turns.text: Tell me how a bicycle stays upright.
Now show me how it steers.

lines.text: path lean stroke=accent thick=1.5 | M80 22 q10 -8 22 0 m-5 -4 l5 4 l-6 3
path steer stroke=accent thick=1.5 | M120 40 q10 4 14 14 m-1 -6 l1 6 l-6 -1
say t1x1 label near=front:below | front wheel steers under the fall

say t1x7 aside | Standing still, none of this works. That is why it falls.

lines.text: say t2x6 label near=bike:above | bike leans left
path fall stroke=lean thick=1.5 | M62 30 q-10 6 -12 18 m-1 -6 l1 6 l6 -2

path steer stroke=accent thick=1.5 | M104 30 q-8 4 -12 12 m0 -6 l0 6 l6 0

say t2x11 aside | Faster means slower, gentler corrections.
say t2x12 choice | why does it self-correct
say t2x13 choice | how do you turn a corner

elements.text: front wheel steers under the fall
A moving bike steers itself upright.
When it leans left, you steer left, so the wheels swing back under the body. Small corrections, constantly, mostly unnoticed.
Speed helps: the faster the wheels turn, the more gentle the corrections needed. Spinning wheels add some gyroscopic stability.
The fork's geometry (trail) makes the front wheel trail behind its steering axis, so it tends to turn into a lean on its own.
Standing still, none of this works. That is why it falls.
